BootstrapBlazor.Shared.Components.Sample.ModalIdeaIntro: The following is for reference only: this approach is influenced by frameworks like WinForm. This example illustrates it.
BootstrapBlazor.Shared.Components.Sample.ModalIdeaP1: The purpose is to show a dialog first, then display the component ResultDialogDemo in the dialog. The business logic is completed in this component. Click the Close button to return Cancel or the Save button to return Ok. This approach is correct and consistent with WinForm. Subsequent logic is handled according to the return value.
BootstrapBlazor.Shared.Components.Sample.ModalIdeaP2: Alternatively, show a dialog first and let ResultDialogDemo handle the business logic. When clicking Close, cancel or roll back, or just close. When clicking Save, persist or process the result then close. This approach is also valid. You don't need to rely on the dialog return value for follow-up logic; moving the business logic into the component inside the dialog is more cohesive and avoids custom return types when modal return values are not enough.
